reading.body:
Alexandria Paolozzi Moore is named on 6 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one lobbying firm, all for a single client, FDD ACTION.

The pattern is narrow and deep rather than broad. Six filings, one firm, one client, and 14 distinct bills named across them. A lobbyist working one client's AI portfolio across that many bills is doing sustained legislative coverage, not a one-off registration. The bills are all dated 2025 or later, so this is current activity, not a historical record.

For AI specifically, this is what the influence layer looks like at the individual level. Compute, buildings, and power set the physical ceiling on AI scaling, but the rules that govern deployment, procurement, and research funding are written by legislators, and lobbyists are the people who carry positions into those offices. The disclosed prior government position, an internship in a House office in 2010, is the only link in this data between the lobbyist and the legislative branch, and the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires it to be listed because it falls within the prior twenty years.

The data does not say what positions were advocated on any bill, whether any bill became law, or how much was spent. It does not identify the other lobbyists on the same filings, and it notes that a different lobbyist shares this name. It covers one person's disclosed AI lobbying footprint and nothing about outcomes.
